newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzanian shilling down on dollar and pound.
newsitem.headline: Tanzanian shilling down on dollar and pound.

text.p: The Tanzanian shilling ended the week down on the dollar after level pegging for more than one week, the Bank of Tanzania said on Friday.
Against the pound, the shilling also finished the week slightly lower, the central bank added.

Central bank dealers quoted a shilling mid-rate of 624.7098 to the dollar compared to Thursday's 624.69, and 1054.8257 to the pound against Thursday's rate of 1053.4179. Last Friday the shilling exchanged at a mean rate of 624.69 versus the dollar.

Senior financial analysts and dealers told Reuters that while the shilling has remained stable for the past week, an expected surge in post-budget business activity will put the local currency under pressure.

"(Business) people are taking stock after the budget -- call it post-budget positioning. What we should expect is decisions taken now will be translated into market action in about two weeks," said one financial analyst.
New business orders will mean demand for foreign exchange which translates into demand for dollars putting downward pressure on the shilling, dealers said.
One said: "An increase in demand for foreign exchange means more demand for dollars which will drive the shilling down."

Demand is expected to catch up with supply around late August or September when the International Monetary Fund (IMF) is likely to inject $30 million into the economy, its second tranche of a $240 million three-year Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility (ESAF).

The World Bank is also expected to start payment of a $120 million Structural Adjustment Credit (SAC) as soon as the government begins privatising the state-run National Bank of Commerce. A timetable is not yet available.
